latest.title: Hierarchical Control of Antiphase Synchronization in Biomorphic Spiking Neural Architectures for Locomotor Control
latest.summary: arXiv:2611.22639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Central pattern generators (CPGs) provide a biologically inspired foundation for adaptive locomotor control, yet systematically characterizing their dynamic regimes in spiking neural networks remains challenging. A composite synchronization metric is developed, integrating phase coherence, amplitude balance, and temporal stability. latest.title: EM-SDTrack: Efficient Multi-Scale Spike-driven Tracking for Event Cameras
latest.summary: arXiv:2611.22700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Event-driven spiking neural networks (SNNs) match the sparse spatiotemporal output of event cameras, making spike-driven trackers highly attractive for neuromorphic edge deployment. However, events reveal a target only through their spatial distribution, whose extent varies more than tenfold within one sequence. Event tracking therefore demands multi-scale representation, which existing spike-driven trackers lack. latest.title: Microtubule plus-end tracking proteins EB1c and MOR1/XMAP215 interact to regulate mitosis and cytokinesis in Arabidopsis.
latest.summary: End-binding protein 1 (EB1) and microtubule (MT) polymerase XMAP215 are core components of the MT plus-end protein network. latest.title: Chloroplast movements in siphonous macroalgae in response to high light and grazing.
latest.summary: Fast cytoplasmic streaming enables extensive chloroplast movements in the giant cells of unicellular, siphonous macroalgae. We studied chloroplast movements by light microscopy, macrophotography and pulse-amplitude-modulated (PAM) chlorophyll a fluorescence in two such algae: Dasycladales Acetabularia acetabulum and Bryopsidales Bryopsis sp. Chemical inhibitors of actin polymerisation and microtubule assembly were used to confirm that the observed effects were controlled by the cytoskeleton. latest.title: BioLM-Score: Language-Prior Conditioned Probabilistic Geometric Potentials for Protein-Ligand Scoring.
latest.summary: Motivation Protein-ligand scoring must address affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening, but these objectives are not necessarily optimized together. latest.title: Addressable Control of Hybrid Spin Qubit in Single-Atom Copper-Modified Fullerene.
latest.summary: Developing high-dimensional solid-state quantum technologies requires overcoming the trade-off between spin dimensionality and quantum coherence. Hybrid spin architectures offer a promising solution to expand the quantum state space bottom-up by combining rapid electronic manipulation with robust nuclear phase memory. However, solid-state hybrid spin materials capable of simultaneously supporting both electron and nuclear spin manipulations remain exceedingly rare. Here, we report a Cu2+ (S = 1/2, I = 3/2) hybrid spin system dispersed in a magnetically silent C60 matrix, in which we not only demonstrate comprehensive coherent control over both electron and nuclear spin degrees of freedom…

latest.title: Integration and annotation of spatial multi-omic data with DIRAC.
latest.summary: Spatial multi-omic technologies measure multiple molecular layers within intact tissues. Two central challenges are vertical integration, which combines different molecular modalities, and horizontal integration, which aligns cell types across studies. Here we show domain invariant representation through adaptive calibration (DIRAC), a geometric deep learning model that unifies these tasks in a generalized domain adaptation framework. DIRAC learns task-discriminative features that are insensitive to domain shifts caused by batch effects, omic modalities or study sites, enabling a shared embedding space and automated cell-type annotation through label transfer from reference datasets.…

items.summary: arXiv:2611.14775v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Graph learning on neuromorphic substrates requires an explicit spiking realization of neighborhood aggregation, supporting control and classification. A degree-dependent inhibitory construction implements Majority through shared control neurons, enabling a complete circuit compilation into SuperNeuroMAT. items.title: Halide Perovskite Heterojunction Crossbar Arrays for Selector-Free Analog In-Memory Computing.
items.summary: Passive memristor crossbars require each cell to suppress sneak-path currents while retaining gradual, reproducible conductance programmability. In halide perovskites, however, sneak-current suppression and analog programmability have rarely been integrated and validated across passive arrays. Fabricated arrays have typically relied on peripheral circuitry to mitigate parasitic currents, whereas self-rectifying analog memristors have largely remained at the single-device level. items.title: Near-infrared optoelectronic synapses based on Yb 3+ /Er 3+ -doped two-dimensional BiOI nanosheets for neuromorphic computing.
items.summary: Optoelectronic memristors have attracted considerable attention owing to their ability to utilize both electrical and optical stimulations for information computing and memory. However, most optoelectronic memristors are sensitive to ultraviolet or visible rather than near-infrared (NIR) light. In this work, Yb 3+ /Er 3+ are directly co-doped into BiOI by a hydrothermal method. Then, NIR optoelectronic synaptic memristors are fabricated based on mechanically exfoliated Yb 3+ /Er 3+ co-doped two-dimensional (2D) BiOI nanosheets. The direct incorporation of Yb 3+ /Er 3+ into BiOI greatly simplifies the device fabrication process and extends the photoresponse range of the BiOI to the NIR.…

items.title: A Plasma eMTBR-Tau Immunoassay for Detection of Advanced Insoluble Tau Pathology.
items.summary: Importance Blood biomarkers that reflect neurofibrillary tau burden, a defining hallmark of Alzheimer disease (AD), remain limited. Endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau 243 (eMTBR-tau243) has shown promise when measured by mass spectrometry; a scalable immunoassay could broaden research access and support clinical evaluation. Objective To determine whether plasma levels of eMTBR-tau measured by a novel immunoassay are associated with tau neurofibrillary tangle pathology defined by neuropathology and tau positron emission tomography (PET). items.title: Full-length β-tubulin sequencing of Trichuris trichiura in South Korea reveals novel variants with a conserved benzimidazole-binding pocket.
items.summary: Background Trichuris trichiura remains difficult to control with benzimidazoles, and the genetic mechanisms underlying treatment response in human populations remain poorly understood. Canonical β-tubulin mutations (F167Y, E198A, F200Y) drive benzimidazole resistance in veterinary nematodes, but their prevalence, distribution, and functional impact in human whipworms are largely uncharacterized. South Korea's current low-transmission status creates an ideal setting to examine present-day parasite lineages after decades of sustained deworming. items.title: Oxygen-Plasma-Induced Surface Reconstruction of WSe 2 Enables Nonvolatile Optoelectronic Synapses for in-Sensor Neuromorphic Vision.
items.summary: Developing neuromorphic visual systems that integrate sensing, memory, and information processing is important for reducing data-transfer overhead in edge vision. 2D WSe 2 offers strong light-matter interaction, but its intrinsically rapid carrier relaxation generally leads to volatile photoresponses that are unfavorable for nonvolatile synaptic weight storage. Here, we develop a two-terminal WSe 2 optoelectronic synapse through carefully controlled oxygen-plasma-induced surface reconstruction. The contact-first, plasma-reconstruction-second strategy employs preformed metal electrodes to physically shield the underlying contact regions while allowing the exposed WSe 2 surface to undergo…

items.title: Voltage-Driven Transition from Steady-State Fluctuations to Phase-Transition Noise in Nanoscale VO2 Devices.
items.summary: We investigate the electrically driven metal-to-insulator transition (MIT) in a nanoscale vanadium dioxide (VO2) Mott memristor through noise spectroscopy and two-dimensional resistor network simulations. Our experiments focus on both the insulating phase as the applied voltage approaches the threshold voltage (set transition) and the metallic phase as the voltage is reduced toward the reset voltage (reset transition). In both regimes, we observe an order-of-magnitude increase in relative current noise near the transition points. To analyze the origin of this noise enhancement, we use simulations that capture the stochastic dynamics of the phase transition. The simulations indicate that…

items.title: Stimulus-Driven Reconfigurable Memristors with Volatile-to-Nonvolatile Transition for Spatiotemporal Neuromorphic Computing.
items.summary: Neuromorphic hardware for spatiotemporal information processing requires both transient dynamics and programmable weight storage, whereas existing implementations typically rely either on heterogeneous integration of volatile dynamic units and nonvolatile memory devices or on compliance-current regulation to reconfigure volatile/nonvolatile operation within a single device, increasing device diversity or peripheral control complexity. This work reports a stimulus-reconfigurable Ag/ZnS/FTO memristor in which the stability of Ag conductive pathways is regulated by the strength and temporal scale of external stimuli, enabling volatile short-term dynamics and nonvolatile conductance modulation…

items.title: Projected Korteweg stresses and fluctuation-induced viscosities: the role of order-parameter conservation.
items.summary: We calculate fluctuation-induced contributions to the shear and configurational bulk viscosities arising from Korteweg stresses in a Gaussian scalar-field theory. items.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models
items.summary: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase domain.
